archetype.name: Pocket Passer (short-area)
archetype.definition: A 6-foot-6 rhythm thrower who stays in the pocket, has no scramble game, and makes his living on quick throws underneath while struggling to push the ball accurately past 10 yards.

report.headline: Hurts is gone; McKee is safe underneath but can't yet threaten downfield.
report.take:
Tanner McKee is no longer a spot starter. The dossier reports Jalen Hurts will likely miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs, so a 2023 sixth-rounder with one start in each of the past three seasons now runs an offense that already ranked 28th in EPA. His first start of 2026, a 25-14 home loss to Carolina, showed what he is right now: 26 of 45, 215 yards, a touchdown, no interceptions, and -0.18 EPA per dropback, 37th of 45 qualifiers. His 4.78 yards per attempt was 44th. He never scrambled and ran once on a designed play for no gain, so this is pure pocket play.

The film profile comes straight from the depth splits. Under 10 air yards he completed 71% at roughly break-even EPA. At 10 yards and beyond he completed 28.6%, at -20.1 CPOE, and went 0-for-4 on throws of 20-plus yards that cost 4.9 points. His intended air yards (8.11) sat 2.55 yards short of the sticks. That combined with a 30.8% third-down conversion rate at an average of 10.8 to go to produce drive after drive that stalled. This is not a one-game quirk. His bad-throw rate ranked 56th of 60 in 2024 and 62nd of 63 in 2025. Inaccuracy on anything beyond the first window is the trait to watch.

The box score flatters him. In one-score game states he was -0.542 EPA per play with a 41.7% completion rate. Trailing by nine or more, against a defense sitting on a lead, he was +0.248 at 76.2%. The touchdown and most of the efficient volume came after the game had tilted. The context is also brutal. Lane Johnson is out for the year, Landon Dickerson missed the game, Saquon Barkley sat with a hamstring injury, and the top two backup tight ends were down. He was hit or sacked on 20.8% of dropbacks. The one healthy security blanket, Dallas Goedert, turned 8 targets into +4.4 EPA, and the middle of the field went 5-for-5.

From here, McKee's ceiling is a competent distributor who keeps the ball out of harm's way, which is what his 2024 cameo (0.31 EPA per play, 2nd that season) hinted at with a full cast around him. His floor is what Carolina saw. Whether Dickerson and Barkley return matters nearly as much as anything he does, because this offense cannot ask him to win outside the numbers.

strengths.title: Clean, accurate in the quick game
strengths.body: On throws under 10 air yards he completed 71% with zero CPOE and a 45% success rate. He did not throw an interception or lose a fumble. It is a real but limited skill: he takes what is there quickly (2.43-second time to throw) and avoids disasters. Some of the clean turnover sheet is the flip side of rarely attacking tight windows downfield.

strengths.title: Middle of the field via Goedert
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers went 5-for-5 at +0.798 EPA. Goedert was the only high-volume target who produced, at +0.545 per target. It is a tiny sample, but it fits his profile: a tall pocket passer seeing the seams and working with the tight end on in-breakers. Leaning into it is the obvious game plan while the receivers outside struggle to get on the same page with him.

strengths.title: Has shown a higher gear
strengths.body: In his 2024 start he posted 0.31 EPA per play and a 54.2% success rate, ranking 2nd and 1st that season. That came in one game with a healthy roster. It proves he can run a functioning offense when protection and the run game hold up. It does not prove he can do it every week.

concerns.title: Accuracy collapses past 10 yards
concerns.body: He completed 28.6% of throws of 10-plus air yards at -20.1 CPOE and went 0-for-4 deep. His CPOE fell 7.8 points from last year's start. Bad-throw rates near the bottom of the league in both prior seasons say this is a persistent trait, not one bad afternoon. Without a credible intermediate and deep threat, defenses can squat on the short game and force long third downs.

concerns.title: Efficiency came in garbage time
concerns.body: When the game was within one score he produced -0.542 EPA per play and completed 41.7%. Trailing by nine-plus he jumped to +0.248 and 76.2%. The touchdown and the respectable yardage were largely handed over by a defense protecting a lead. That split, more than the final line, is the honest read on his starting form.

concerns.title: Depleted line and backfield
concerns.body: Lane Johnson is out for the season, Dickerson missed the Carolina game, and Barkley sat. The run game ranks 27th in EPA, which kept McKee in long-yardage spots and got him hit or sacked on over a fifth of his dropbacks. Dickerson and Barkley carry expected return dates for this week. Johnson does not, so the right side stays a problem regardless.

trend.note: There is one 2026 start, so there is no path to follow yet. His three career starts have swung from excellent (2024) to middling (2025) to poor (2026), and the deciding variable has been the cast around him more than any growth arc.

nextGame.headline: Dallas's leaky pass defense is the soft landing he needs
nextGame.body:
Dallas ranks 32nd in pass EPA allowed and 31st in EPA on short throws. That second number is the key one, because short throws are the one area where McKee was functional against Carolina. The Cowboys also rank 28th in sack rate and in hit rate, which should ease some pressure on a line missing Johnson. They have been worst-in-class against tight ends (0.61 EPA per target allowed, 30th), lining up directly with the Goedert connection. Quarterbacks have averaged 21.3 PPR points against them, 28th. Game script also helps volume: Dallas's offense ranks 6th in EPA, the Book has the Cowboys favored by 4.5, and an Eagles defense ranked 25th probably can't keep this low-scoring.

On the Dallas side, CB Cobie Durant (62% of snaps) is out and LB Dee Winters (61%) is doubtful with an Achilles sprain. Losing Winters thins the underneath coverage McKee will be throwing into. DeMarvion Overshown is listed out but reported on track to play. For Philadelphia, Dickerson and Barkley both carry return dates for this game, and their status is the swing. A healthy Barkley gives McKee early-down efficiency and play-action, while a returning Dickerson steadies the interior. Without them, a favorable matchup still runs through long third downs.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game vs. Dallas's soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: McKee's offense lives under 10 yards, and Dallas allows a 0.268 EPA on short throws, 31st in the league. With Winters likely out, the linebacker level is thinner still. This is the matchup where his completion rate should rebound toward his short-area level.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against the worst TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Goedert was McKee's only consistently productive target, and Dallas ranks 30th in EPA per target allowed to tight ends. With Stowers and Calcaterra hurt, Goedert should see heavy usage. Expect the Eagles to script seam and over routes to him early.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script forces the ball downfield
keyMatchups.body: Dallas's offense ranks 6th in EPA and passes above expectation, and Philadelphia's defense ranks 25th. If the Eagles fall behind, McKee has to throw outside the numbers, where he has been at his worst. Dallas does allow explosive passes freely (31st), so there is upside if he hits even a couple.

nextGame.watch: Whether McKee completes anything 15-plus yards outside the numbers to DeVonta Smith. If Dallas's 31st-ranked explosive-pass defense can't coax that out of him, nobody will.

restOfSeason.body:
McKee is the starter for the foreseeable future, and the volume is real: 45 attempts in his first start, and a defense that will put him in catch-up mode. Expect yardage that looks fine on paper, with efficiency below league average. He will throw short accurately and avoid turnovers, but his multi-season bad-throw history says the downfield accuracy gap won't close quickly. Realistic weekly output is roughly 200 to 260 passing yards and one or two touchdowns, with a lot of sacks, because he does not escape the pocket and the right tackle spot is compromised all year.

What regresses: the zero interceptions. Attempting this many passes with this accuracy profile will produce picks; his 2025 start had one. What could improve: the supporting cast. Barkley's and Dickerson's returns would give him the early-down efficiency and play-action his 2024 start was built on. Soft matchups like Dallas can produce a 2024-style game, but on average he grades as a low-end starter whose numbers depend on volume and script.
swingFactors: Game script from a 25th-ranked Eagles defense

confidence.note: One 2026 start, three career starts total, and a supporting cast changing week to week.
